result:
Typing `@someone` in a comment becomes an inbox row only after the handle is resolved to a member `UserId`, that id is carried on the `comment.created` event, and `notify` decides the row is worth writing. Mail is a later, separate pass.

## 1. The handle is the local part of a member’s email

On the issue page (`src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/projects/[projectSlug]/issues/[issueNumber]/page.tsx`) the composer receives the first 100 live members from `listMembers` (`src/server/services/member-service.ts` → `memberRepo.listMembers`). `MentionTextarea` (`src/components/domain/comment/mention-textarea.tsx`) uses `findMentionQuery`, `matchMembers`, and `mentionHandle` in `src/components/domain/comment/mention-query.ts` for the autocomplete. `mentionHandle` is `email.split("@")[0].toLowerCase()`. Accepting a suggestion runs `applyMention`, which inserts `@` plus that local part.

Every keystroke also calls `resolveMentions(body, members)` from `src/lib/mentions.ts`. `CommentComposer` keeps the resulting `UserId`s and submits them as `mentionedUserIds` on `CreateCommentInput`. `createCommentSchema` in `src/schemas/comment.ts` allows at most 50 of those ids. That client list is a hint. The server parses the body again.

## 2. Posting the comment re-resolves the handles

`createCommentAction` (`src/actions/comments/create-comment.ts`) goes through `withAction`, which parses the schema and loads the `Actor`. The action then checks `can(actor, "comment:create")`, charges the `comment:create` rate limit, and calls `createComment`.

`createComment` in `src/server/services/comment-service.ts` checks org scope, loads the issue, checks `comment:create` again, rejects an archived issue, and charges the same rate limit a second time. It then calls `resolveMentionedUsers`:

- `memberRepo.listMembers` loads up to `MENTION_LOOKUP_LIMIT` (100) live members, newest first. Archived members are excluded.
- `resolveMentions(body, members)` builds a map with `handleOf`: the lowercased local part of `member.user.email` → `member.userId`. If two members share a local part, the later row in that page wins.
- `extractMentions` strips fenced blocks and inline code, then matches `@handle` only at the start of the text or after whitespace or `([<`. The handle is lowercased, must be 2–40 characters of `[a-z0-9._-]`, and duplicates are dropped. An address like `alice@example.com` is not a mention. An unknown handle is dropped and does not fail the write.
- The returned list is the union of those server ids and any client-supplied ids that belong to someone in that same 100-member page. A client id for anyone else is discarded.

`commentRepo.insertComment` stores that list as JSON on the comment. `emit("comment.created", …)` then publishes the same `mentionedUserIds` on the event, next to `actorEnvelope(actor)` (`orgId`, `actorId`, `occurredAt`), `commentId`, and `issueId`. The payload type is `TaskflowEventMap["comment.created"]` in `src/types/event.ts`. Editing a comment does not run this path: `updateComment` neither re-resolves mentions nor emits `comment.created`.

## 3. The event carries the list to the fan-out

`emit` in `src/lib/event-bus.ts` delivers the payload to every subscriber with `Promise.allSettled`, so a failing listener does not roll back the comment. The notification listener is attached at process start: `instrumentation.register` imports `event-registry`, which imports `src/server/services/notification-service.ts`, and that module calls `registerFanOut()` on load. `registerFanOut` does `subscribe("comment.created", …)`.

That handler loads the issue and does two `notify` calls. The first is kind `comment_created`, sent to the issue author and assignee. The second runs only when `mentionedUserIds.length > 0`: kind `comment_mention`, recipients exactly `payload.mentionedUserIds`, title `"You were mentioned"`, href `/issues/${issueId}`, `actorId` the commenter. The fan-out reads the event list. It does not parse the comment body again.

## 4. What becomes an inbox row

`notify` (`notification-service.ts`) loads the org so it can build a `FlagContext` (plan, flag overrides). For each distinct recipient:

- If `recipientId === payload.actorId`, it skips. Mentioning yourself writes nothing.
- `preferenceRepo.getPreference(orgId, recipientId, "comment_mention")` loads the preference. `null` means the person has never set one.
- `resolveChannels(preference, flags)` picks the channels:
  - No preference: `["in_app", "email"]` (`DEFAULT_CHANNELS`).
  - Otherwise `in_app` is included when `preference.inApp` is true.
  - `email` is included when `preference.email` is true and either `digestOnly` is false or `isEnabled("digest_email", flags)` is true. `digest_email` is a plan flag with minimum plan `growth` (`src/config/feature-flags.ts`), and an org override can turn it on.
- An empty channel list skips the recipient. No row is inserted.
- Otherwise `notificationRepo.insertNotifications` writes one `notifications` row: kind `comment_mention`, the title and body above, `readAt` null, and `channels` stored as JSON.

The inbox does not look at `channels`. `listNotifications` filters by org, recipient, optional unread flag, and optional kind. Any inserted row shows up in three places, all of which call that function for `actor.userId`:

- The shell in `src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/layout.tsx` uses `notifications.total` as the unread badge.
- `src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/inbox/page.tsx` renders `NotificationList` after `can(actor, "notification:read")`.
- The `@panel` notifications page lists the latest 20.

So the four outcomes at write time are:

- **Nothing.** The handle never became a `UserId`, the recipient is the author, or their `comment_mention` preference yields no channels (`inApp` false, and email withheld because email is off, or because `digestOnly` is on while `digest_email` is off).
- **An inbox row with `in_app` only.** `inApp` is true and the email rule above fails.
- **An inbox row with `email` only.** `inApp` is false and the email rule passes. The row still appears in the inbox, because the inbox query ignores `channels`.
- **An inbox row with both channels.** The default when they have no preference, and also when both switches allow it. With `digestOnly` true this still includes `email` only while `digest_email` is enabled.

A mentioned assignee who did not write the comment also gets the separate `comment_created` row from the first `notify` in the same handler.

## 5. What actually sends email

`notify` records the `email` channel and stops. It never calls `sendEmail`, and nothing on this path renders `MentionEmail` (`src/emails/mention-email.tsx`) or the `"mention"` case in `src/emails/render.ts`.

The mail that can include this row is the daily digest. `startScheduler` (`src/server/jobs/scheduler.ts`), started from `instrumentation.register`, enqueues a `digest-email` job about once an hour; `POST /api/cron/digest` can run the same job. `runDigestEmailJob` (`src/server/jobs/digest-email-job.ts`) handles an org only when the UTC hour equals `org.settings.digestHourUtc` and `isEnabled("digest_email", …)` is true. Recipients come from `listDigestRecipients` → `listDigestSubscribers`: users with `digestOnly` on at least one kind, not necessarily `comment_mention`. `buildDigest` (`src/server/services/digest-service.ts`) takes their unread notifications in the last day, up to `DIGEST_MAX_ENTRIES` (50), with no filter on kind or channel. `renderDigest` calls `renderEmail("digest")`, and `sendEmail` (`src/server/services/email-service.ts`) logs the draft. Each included notification is then marked read so the next run skips it.

A person who has never saved preferences gets the inbox row immediately and is not a digest subscriber, so no mail goes out. A digest subscriber gets that row folded into the digest email at the org’s digest hour, while `digest_email` is on and the row is still unread.
